thread:
ProductOps: @channel Heads-up — scheduled rolling maintenance for network egress/firewall rule updates. Window: 2026-03-17 02:00-04:00 UTC. We expect short (up to ~3-6 minutes) client request interruptions per-region while rules roll. No persistent data loss expected. :calendar:

ProductOps: Reason: updating egress rules to unblock an upstream provider and reduce cross-region latency spikes we've seen on heavy token streams. This change touches the hosted API control plane and the edge NAT rules; Dedicated pools will be touched for routing only (no GPU VM restarts).

ProductOps: Impact summary (TL;DR):
- Hosted API: transient 1-6m 503/524s possible during each region's rule swap.
- Dedicated: routing flaps possible for a few requests; no model restarts expected.
- Private (VPC): no changes unless customer opted into shared egress.

ProductOps: Action items: please ensure on-call coverage for the window, post the maintenance object to status.redwood.com before we start, and copy the customer notification below for Support.

oncall-bot: Scheduled maintenance created — MNT-2026-0317-01. Reminder set 30m before window. Paging schedule assigned to SRE rotation.

SRE Raj: Will take primary during the window. Can someone confirm the exact IP ranges and the pre/post validation steps? I want the runbook in this thread.

ProductOps: IP ranges: `34.82.0.0/16, 34.83.0.0/16, 104.154.0.0/15` (published to infra.kb). Pre-checks:
```
- curl -sS https://status.redwood.com/health || echo "status unreachable"
- check traffic from canary-vpc: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY_TOKEN" https://api.redwood.com/v1/health
- list NAT rules: gcloud compute firewall-rules list --filter="name~'egress-redwood'"
```
Post-checks:
```
- validate 95th pct latency back to baseline: datadog query `avg:api.request.duration{env:prod}.rollup(5m)`
- run a small synthetic token stream test: `python tests/synthetics/stream_test.py --profile=regions`
```

Support Maria: I'll prepare the customer e-mail and status page message. Need a short subject + body we can paste. Also list of enterprise customers with dedicated network peering that we should ping directly.

ProductOps: Customer templates below — feel free to edit.
---
Subject: Planned maintenance — short service interruptions expected (Mar 17 UTC)

Body:
Hello —

We are performing a short, rolling network maintenance on Mar 17, 02:00-04:00 UTC to update egress/firewall rules. Some API requests may see brief errors (approx 1-6 minutes) during regional rule switches. We do not expect persistent outages or data loss. If you have a dedicated networking setup or peering, our Support team will reach out directly.

If you rely on strict SLAs during that window and need assistance, please reply to this message and we will provide a scoped mitigation plan.

Thanks,
Redwood Support Team
---

Status page message (short):
"Planned maintenance: rolling network egress updates. Expect short, intermittent request failures (1-6m) per region between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC on Mar 17. We'll update when complete."
---

Customer Success Theo: I'll prepare the enterprise notification list and DM Support with high-priority accounts to phone.

Eng Li: I'll be on standby for quick rollback of the rule push if we see >10% sustained error rate for 10+ minutes. Rollback command is `gcloud compute firewall-rules update egress-redwood --source-ranges=OLD_RANGE` (runbook step 7).

deploy-bot: Rolling update job queued — job id `roll-egress-1769537890`. Canary push scheduled in `us-west1` first.

SRE Raj: Copying runbook steps I will execute during the window:
1) Pre-checks complete 20m before start.
2) Create snapshot of firewall config.
3) Push rule to canary region `us-west1`. Wait 5m, run synthetics.
4) If canary good, sequentially apply to `europe-west1`, `asia-east1`, `us-central1`. Pause 3-5m between regions.
5) Monitor: error rate, token stream tails, KV cache miss spikes.
6) If error > 7% for two consecutive monitoring windows (5m each), initiate rollback.
7) Post-change validate traffic and mark maintenance complete.

Support Maria: Drafting customer messages now. Will post to status page once ProductOps approves copy.

ProductOps: Approved. Please post to status page 15 minutes before maintenance start. Use the short status copy above.

oncall-bot: Reminder — 30m until scheduled maintenance (MNT-2026-0317-01). Paging on-call: SRE Raj, then SRE rotation.

SRE Raj: Pre-checks done, canary token stream looks normal. Proceeding to canary push in 2m.

deploy-bot: Canary push started in `us-west1` (job roll-egress-1769537890-canary). Logs: https://internal-logs.redwood.com/roll-egress/1769537890/canary

Support Maria: Status page updated: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/MNT-2026-0317-01 — short message posted and customer email queued.

SRE Raj: Canary looks good. Latency stable, synthetic stream OK. Proceeding to europe.

Eng Li: Monitoring infra — no regressions observed.

SRE Raj: Europe done, asia started. Minor 502 spike in `asia-east1` for ~90s during rule switch, recovered automatically, error rate peaked at 2.8%. No rollback.

ProductOps: Noted. Posting interim update on status page: "Canary successful; rolling through regions. Minor brief errors in asia-east1; traffic recovered automatically. No customer action required."

Customer Success Theo: Pinging top 10 enterprise customers by phone per plan. No escalations so far.

SRE Raj: Final region complete. Running post-checks now.

SRE Raj: Post-checks: API latency within expected range, synthetic stream stable, no KV cache anomalies.

ProductOps: Maintenance complete — closing MNT-2026-0317-01. Summary for status page and CS: rolling egress/firewall rule update completed successfully. Intermittent errors (max ~90s in asia-east1) observed but recovered; no customer-facing incidents opened. Marking as resolved. :white_check_mark:

oncall-bot: Maintenance MNT-2026-0317-01 marked complete. Follow-up tasks: add a note to infra.kb, schedule a retro if any post-change anomalies surface.

Support Maria: Sent final customer notification (template updated to include observed 90s spike in asia-east1).

ProductOps: Thanks everyone. I'll drop a short internal postmortem in `incidents/` if anything notable emerges, otherwise this will be a maintenance note only.

Eng Li: Leaving a quick snippet for runbook improvements: add an automated rollback if sustained error >5% for 10m, and increase canary wait to 8m in asia regions.

SRE Raj: Agreed — noted in runbook.

ProductOps: End of thread — great execution. :tada:
